+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8e80'
+title: 'Stub script step "permission": the run sends session/request_permission and waits for the outcome, also in a child run'
+---
+## What
+Request from the ACP client session (foundationmodelsacpclient-11). It blocks the client card ^kg9t45m, items B1 and B2. Today the stub script has the steps `text`, `reasoning`, `toolCall`, `gate` and `elicit` (see `Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Configuration/ScriptedStubScript.swift`). No agent code calls `requestPermission`.
+
+Needed: a step `{"permission": "<title>"}`. The run sends `session/request_permission` to the client, waits for the outcome, and goes on after it. A cancelled outcome ends the pass (as `elicit` does with a decline or a cancel). It must work in a CHILD run too, so that the client can check that the request shows under the child session id exactly once and never under the root.
+
+## Do
+1. Read how `elicit` works end to end (`ScriptedPassStep.elicit`, `ScriptedSessionBackend.askUser`, `ScriptedElicitation`, `ElicitationRelay` / `ElicitationClaims`, the child elicitation under the child session id of ^my9mbdf). Find what the host has to send a permission request to the client under a given session id: the ACP connection API for `session/request_permission`, its request and response types in the FoundationModelsACP package, and how a child session id is used as the session id of the request (a child is its own session on the wire).
+2. Add the step `permission` to the script grammar (`ScriptedStubScript`, a `ScriptedPassStep` case, the playbook), parse and document it in the grammar comment at the top of `ScriptedStubScript.swift`. The request carries the title and a small set of options (allow once, reject once, or whatever the ACP schema in the checkout defines; read it). The outcome is one of: selected option (the pass goes on), cancelled (the pass ends, as for `elicit`).
+3. In a child run, the request goes out under the child session id, exactly once, never under the root. Use the same routing as the child elicitation (claims, relay). Cancel semantics: `session/cancel` of the child while a permission request is pending cancels the request (the outcome is cancelled).
+4. Do not change a sibling package; if a host API is missing in FoundationModelsACP, mark the task stuck and say exactly which.
+5. Docs: add the step to the stub script section of README.md (ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English).
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] A script with `{"permission":"..."}` in the root session sends exactly one `session/request_permission` under the root id, waits, and plays the rest after a selected outcome.
+- [ ] A cancelled outcome ends the pass.
+- [ ] In a child run, the request shows under the child session id exactly once and never under the root id.
+- [ ] `session/cancel` of the child while a request is pending ends the request with the cancelled outcome.
+- [ ] The grammar comment and the README name the step.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Unit tests over the in-process wire (the existing fixtures with a scripted client that answers or cancels the request), including a child run with a gate/hold so that the request is pending when the cancel arrives.
+- [ ] Run the touched unit suites. Do NOT run the IntegrationTests package (CI only).
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd`. #subagents
\ No newline at end of file

+
+> Scope: `review sha ebd9069~1..ebd9069` — reviewed the diffs only — lines this change added or modified. 9 file(s) reviewed, 1 not reviewed.
+
+> 1 file(s) not reviewed — no validator matched:
+> - `README.md` — no validator matches this file
+
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Configuration/ScriptedPermission.swift:62` `reuse/reuse` — ScriptedPermission.runCodeArguments(asking:) repeats the behavior of ScriptedElicitation.runCodeArguments(asking:). Both encode the title or message as a JSON literal, wrap the snippet in a runCode arguments dictionary, and return the JSON text. The duplicate is a parallel copy of an existing function that is almost what this step needs, so a later fix to one path would not reach the other. Generalize ScriptedElicitation.runCodeArguments so it takes the question's schema and reply handling as parameters, or move the shared encoding and dictionary wrapping into one helper that both ScriptedElicitation and ScriptedPermission call. Keep each case's specific snippet text in its own file.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Configuration/ScriptedPermission.swift:74` `reuse/reuse` — ScriptedPermission.snippet(asking:) is a near-copy of ScriptedElicitation.snippet(asking:). Both check for the elicit global, return the refusal marker with Refusal.unavailable, encode the title or message, call elicit, and map a non-accept reply to the refusal marker. Only the request shape and the accepted value differ, so the copy diverges from the canonical sandbox-question path. Parameterize the snippet builder in ScriptedElicitation with the requestedSchema and the accepted-value expression, then call that shared builder from ScriptedPermission with the permission field and its schema. This keeps one implementation of the refusal and marker logic.
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Configuration/ScriptedSessionBackend.swift:466` `duplication/duplication` — The new `.permission` case in `play` repeats the `.elicit` case. Both compute the `runCode` arguments, call `askUser`, and return when the user gave no answer. Only the argument builder differs. Two copies of the same control flow can drift apart, for example if one later gains a yield or a lock. Merge the two cases into one helper or one case. For example, add a private function that maps a question step (`elicit` or `permission`) to its `runCode` arguments, then run one `askUser` call for both. This keeps the control flow in one place. The step-to-arguments mapping can stay per step.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTestSupport/RecordingClient.swift:105` `reuse/reuse` — ElicitationWireRecorder.recordPermission(request:) repeats the append-under-watch pattern of recordCreate(request:). Both append to a WatchedValue through update, so the same behavior is written twice in one actor. Add one generic private helper, for example record(_:into:) over a WatchedValue<[Element]>, and call it from both recordCreate and recordPermission. Alternatively, keep the two one-line methods and note that they share the pattern.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTestSupport/RecordingClient.swift:119` `reuse/reuse` — ElicitationWireRecorder.waitForPermissions(count:) repeats the count-based wait of waitForCreates(count:) on a different WatchedValue. The two waits differ only in the element type and the label, so the same wait logic lives in two places. Make one generic helper, for example waitForCount<Element>(_ watched: WatchedValue<[Element]>, count: Int, label: String), and let both waitForCreates and waitForPermissions call it.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/ScriptedPermissionStepTests.swift:80` `swift/optionals` — A test reads the recorder with `?? []`. If the recorder is nil, the test uses an empty list instead of stopping with a clear failure. The rule asks for an unwrap with an assertion in a test. Replace the fallback with `let recorder = try #require(run.fixture.harness.elicitations)` and read `await recorder.permissions` from it.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/ScriptedPermissionStepTests.swift:208` `swift/concurrency` — The root prompt runs in an unstructured `Task` whose handle is discarded (`_ = Task { … }`). The task is never stored, awaited, or cancelled, and any error it throws is lost. The prompt stays open until the child ends, so the test cannot tell whether the prompt failed. Store the handle (for example `let rootPrompt = Task { … }`) on `AskingRun`. Cancel it in the fixture close path, and await `rootPrompt.value` after the child ends, so a thrown error fails the test.
